To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the broadcast time of segmented messages scales as O(nk-1/k) as opposed to O(logn) for the unsegmented case, where k is the number of segments in a message, and the broadcast time can be improved further by introducing giveup and pull techniques.
the time taken for broadcast of a single message in an epidemic manner scales as log n and for segmented message it scales as nk-11k.

message segmentation has a negative impact on the broadcast time and number of redundant contacts, and the use of giveup and the optimal d in the push and pull techniques can reduce the broadcast time and the number of redundant contacts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of message fragmentation on message dissemination time and number of contacts incurred in the process.
the effect of message fragmentation on broadcast time in dynamic networks.

the following aspects: (a) understanding the impact of message segmentation on the efficiency and speed of message broadcast, (b) proposing variants of existing techniques to further improve broadcast efficiency and speed and (c) providing suggestions for network designers to improve network performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the message segmentation technique is very useful for broadcast in dynamic networks.
message segmentation is an effective technique to reduce the time of broadcast and also to reduce the total number of contacts incurred during message dissemination.
the message segmentation is a good approach in terms of reducing the total number of redundant connections, but it increases the broadcast time significantly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
segmentation of messages can be used to improve the broadcast time and reduce number of useless contacts in dynamic networks.

the message segmentation is a very effective technique to improve message broadcast in large scale networks, however, it is important to design a suitable segmentation technique and also to choose a proper topology for a given network size.
message segmentation does not necessarily lead to a better performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the broadcast time can be improved by a factor of k in the case of segmented messages as opposed to the single message epidemic approach.
message segmentation has significant impact on the speed of message dissemination and hence network designers should take it into account.
message segmentation has a significant impact on broadcast time and total number of redundant connections incurred during the transmission process.
